payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: Minimal support in R-learner does not outweigh failures in other models.
themes.interpretation: Thyromegaly presence shows negligible or inconsistent signaling across all roles.
themes.name: Thyroid Examination

themes.disagreements: Consistent evidence across univariable and predictive forest models for both treatment and outcome, with no significant effect modification signal.
themes.interpretation: Strong evidence of a common cause for both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Cumulative Tobacco Exposure

themes.disagreements: Strong effect modification signals in TTF1 contrast with very weak or absent signals for general TP53 mutation status and specific R273H variants.
themes.interpretation: Molecular markers showing differential treatment effects, particularly TTF-1 protein expression.
themes.name: Tumor Molecular Profiling

themes.disagreements: Transependymal flow shows high consistency for outcome prognosis; bilirubin provides a much weaker signal.
themes.interpretation: Clinical and laboratory markers serving as prognostic factors for the outcome without significant treatment-association signals.
themes.name: Prognostic Clinical Indicators

themes.disagreements: Signals for treatment goals, response, and cycle frequency are fragmented across folds and models, failing to establish a stable role.
themes.interpretation: Treatment-related documentation and scoring metrics with insufficient evidence to be identified as confounders or modifiers.
themes.name: Treatment Context and Response

themes.disagreements: Ventricular edema (339) shows no treatment prediction support in predictive forests, unlike vasogenic edema (338) and hemorrhage (340).
themes.interpretation: Neuroimaging markers of CNS involvement showing strong prognostic importance and significant treatment-effect heterogeneity.
themes.name: Intracranial Imaging Findings

themes.disagreements: TMB (334) shows strong effect modification signals but relatively weak treatment prediction compared to VAF (337); tumor cell presence (331) lacks consistent signal across models.
themes.interpretation: Pathologic and genetic markers exhibiting a mixture of prognostic value, treatment selection bias, and effect modification.
themes.name: Tumor Histology and Genomics

themes.disagreements: Ulceration (335) lacks the strong prognostic signal seen in unintended weight change (336).
themes.interpretation: Systemic markers of patient health prior to treatment with strong prognostic and effect-modifying signals.
themes.name: Clinical Systemic State

themes.disagreements: who_grade lacks strong effect modification evidence compared to the stronger prognostic and treatment signals for ventricular size and vertebral metastasis.
themes.interpretation: Indicators of tumor burden and neuro-oncological severity, consistently linked to outcome and treatment selection.
themes.name: Neuro-oncological Burden

themes.disagreements: Vitamin deficiency anemia shows more distributed evidence across univariable and penalized models, while WBC count is strongly captured by the predictive forest.
themes.interpretation: Systemic hematologic markers reflecting overall patient health and potential for treatment response modification.
themes.name: Systemic Hematologic State

themes.disagreements: Visual field deficit only exhibits evidence of effect modification, lacking the confounding roles seen in weight and wheezing.
themes.interpretation: General clinical physical findings and constitutional status.
themes.name: General Physical Findings

themes.disagreements: Vinorelbine administration has more robust evidence for effect modification (causal forest) than vitamin supplement use, which acts primarily as a weak confounder.
themes.interpretation: Prior pharmacological interventions and supplementation status.
themes.name: Prior Pharmacological History

themes.disagreements: Weak, inconsistent support for treatment prediction and outcome prognosis across predictive forests; complete lack of support in univariable and penalized main/interaction models.
themes.interpretation: Candidates related to prior therapeutic interventions (radiation and drug dosing) exhibiting complementary signals for effect modification in R-learner and causal forest models, despite minimal evidence for main effects.
themes.name: Prior Therapeutic Interventions

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
